title_en: Liu Xinglin v. Hai Gang Rural Credit Cooperative — deposit dispute

full_text_en:
Liu Xinglin v. Haigang Rural Credit Cooperative — Deposit Dispute

Plaintiff: Liu Xinglin, male, 51 years old, residing in Xigang Town, Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Song Zhenjiang and Ning Xiuwei, lawyers of Handan Branch of Hebei Tianjie Law Firm.

Defendant: Haigang Rural Credit Cooperative of Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province. Domicile: Middle Section of Gangcheng Street, Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City.

Legal Representative: Zhang Wenjiang, Director of the Cooperative.

Agent ad litem: Xu Deli, staff member of the Suburban Rural Credit Cooperative Union of Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Mingguang, lawyer of Beijing Jinheng Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Liu Xinglin, filed a lawsuit with the Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province regarding a deposit dispute with the defendant, Haigang Rural Credit Cooperative of Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province (hereinafter referred to as Haigang Credit Cooperative).

The plaintiff alleged: The plaintiff opened a deposit account with the defendant's predecessor, Mafang Rural Credit Cooperative of Qinhuangdao City (the name previously used by the defendant Haigang Credit Cooperative, hereinafter referred to as Mafang Credit Cooperative), and as of July 16, 1998, the total deposit amounted to RMB 1.8 million. On that day, when the plaintiff needed funds and went to the cooperative to withdraw money, he discovered that all the deposits had been misappropriated by the cooperative. At that time, Cheng Xiuli, the director of the cooperative, wrote a "Certificate" for me, stamped with the cooperative's official seal, guaranteeing full repayment by August of that year. Thereafter, despite repeated demands by the plaintiff, no results were achieved. The plaintiff requested a judgment ordering the defendant to return the RMB 1.8 million deposit misappropriated through infringement and to pay the late payment fee for this amount after September 1, 1998.

The defendant argued: The withdrawal vouchers stamped with the plaintiff's seal confirmed that all deposits had indeed been withdrawn by the plaintiff. The plaintiff's act of leaving his seal with Cheng Xiuli, the former director of the cooperative, constituted an entrustment and authorization by the plaintiff to Cheng Xiuli, and was unrelated to the cooperative. As for the "Certificate" dated July 16, 1998, not only did Cheng Xiuli deny it, but the amount of debt recorded in the "Certificate" also did not match the result of the later audit, so it could not be considered true. The plaintiff's claim was unfounded and should be dismissed.

The Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

From August 1992 to September 1996, the plaintiff, Liu Xinglin, successively deposited RMB 3,615,512.02 with Mafang Credit Cooperative. The defendant, Haigang Credit Cooperative, claimed that this entire amount had been withdrawn by Liu Xinglin. Of the withdrawal vouchers submitted by Haigang Credit Cooperative, Liu Xinglin acknowledged RMB 1,949,325.20; Liu Xinglin did not acknowledge RMB 1,487,800 worth of withdrawal vouchers because they only bore Liu Xinglin's seal but not his signature. Liu Xinglin submitted a "Certificate" issued by Mafang Credit Cooperative on July 16, 1998, which stated: Since opening an account in our cooperative in 1992, Liu Xinglin's current deposit has reached RMB 1.8 million. This amount has been loaned out by our cooperative. We are currently actively and vigorously recovering it, striving to recover all of it by August to repay Liu Xinglin, in order to facilitate his purchase of real estate. This is hereby certified. Cheng Xiuli, the former director of Mafang Credit Cooperative, denied that the cooperative had ever issued such a "Certificate" to Liu Xinglin. During the trial, Haigang Credit Cooperative submitted a "Certificate" issued by Hongyan Industrial Company of Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, certifying that the company had borrowed RMB 600,000 from Liu Xinglin's account with his consent. Based on this, Haigang Credit Cooperative argued that this evidence was sufficient to prove that Liu Xinglin's RMB 1,487,800 deposit was either withdrawn with his consent or loaned out by himself. Liu Xinglin denied the content of the certificate from Hongyan Industrial Company of Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City.

The Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court held: The focus of the dispute between the parties was the whereabouts of the RMB 1,487,800 deposit. The defendant, Haigang Credit Cooperative, based on withdrawal vouchers bearing the plaintiff Liu Xinglin's seal but not his signature, claimed that the entire amount had been withdrawn by Liu Xinglin; Liu Xinglin, based on withdrawal vouchers bearing both his seal and signature, the fact that his seal had indeed been left with Cheng Xiuli, and the certificate from Mafang Credit Cooperative, claimed that the withdrawal vouchers with only a seal but no signature were not his doing, and that this sum had been misappropriated by Mafang Credit Cooperative. In view of the fact that the deposit relationship between Liu Xinglin and Haigang Credit Cooperative was genuine, and that the withdrawal vouchers submitted by Haigang Credit Cooperative were of two types—those with a seal but no signature and those with both seal and signature—and that Liu Xinglin's seal had indeed been kept with Cheng Xiuli, Haigang Credit Cooperative had the responsibility to prove that the amounts on the withdrawal vouchers with a seal but no signature were also withdrawn by Liu Xinglin. Haigang Credit Cooperative did not submit evidence in this regard, so the withdrawal or lending of the deposit could not be determined based on the withdrawal vouchers with a seal but no signature. Haigang Credit Cooperative should pay Liu Xinglin this portion of the deposit and the interest. Haigang Credit Cooperative's refusal to pay constituted an infringement of Liu Xinglin's property rights. Article 117 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Anyone who encroaches on the property of the State, a collective, or another person shall return the property; if the property cannot be returned, compensation shall be made at an estimated price." Article 108 provides: "Debts shall be cleared. If a debtor is temporarily unable to repay a debt, the debtor may repay it in installments with the consent of the creditor or a ruling by a people's court. If a debtor is able to repay but refuses to do so, the people's court shall compel repayment by judgment." Haigang Credit Cooperative should bear the civil liability to return Liu Xinglin's deposit of RMB 1,487,800 and shall pay the interest due on this amount after September 1, 1998. Accordingly, the Qinhuangdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 29, 2001:

The defendant, Haigang Credit Cooperative, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, pay the plaintiff, Liu Xinglin, a deposit of RMB 1,487,800 and interest (interest calculated from September 1, 1998, until the date this judgment becomes legally effective, at the corresponding period's personal demand deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China).

Litigation cost of RMB 20,184 shall be borne by the plaintiff Liu Xinglin in the amount of RMB 2,018.4, and by the defendant Haigang Credit Cooperative in the amount of RMB 18,165.6.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, both parties were dissatisfied and appealed to the Hebei High People's Court.

The grounds for appeal by Haigang Credit Cooperative were: The withdrawal vouchers confirmed that our cooperative no longer holds any deposit of Liu Xinglin. According to the bank's regulations on deposits and withdrawals, depositors withdraw money by seal, not by personal signature. All withdrawal vouchers submitted by our cooperative bear Liu Xinglin's personal seal, so our cooperative's disbursement of funds was without fault. Liu Xinglin's act of leaving his seal with Cheng Xiuli constituted an authorization to Cheng Xiuli. If there was any harmful act, it should be Cheng Xiuli who is responsible to Liu Xinglin, not the credit cooperative. In fact, Liu Xinglin was aware of all deposits and withdrawals, and all amounts not yet repaid were loaned out by Liu Xinglin himself. Liu Xinglin should directly claim from the borrowers. Liu Xinglin's deposit was not RMB 1.8 million, and the so-called "Certificate" of Mafang Credit Cooperative did not match the facts. The judgment of first instance was erroneous and should be reversed to dismiss Liu Xinglin's claims.

The grounds for appeal by Liu Xinglin were: After August 1998, Haigang Credit Cooperative used my deposits to make loans. For the interest after that time, the judgment of first instance incorrectly calculated interest at the personal demand deposit rate; it should have been calculated at the loan interest rate or at the standard of 0.04% per day. My claim in the first instance was for a judgment ordering the defendant to return RMB 1.8 million in deposits misappropriated through infringement; the first instance determined RMB 1,487,800. After the first instance judgment, I found another deposit certificate dated July 23, 1992, in the amount of RMB 259,936.6, which Haigang Credit Cooperative should pay. Adding this amount still does not exceed my claim in the first instance.

The Hebei High People's Court, upon trial, in addition to confirming the facts found in the first instance, also found:

The appellant Liu Xinglin described the process of issuing the Mafang Credit Cooperative "Certificate" as follows: When I went to withdraw money, Cheng Xiuli said that my money had been loaned out. After reconciliation, there was still RMB 1.8 million of mine in the account. I requested the credit cooperative to write a certificate. Cheng Xiuli told me to write it, so I wrote the certificate, and Cheng Xiuli took out the official seal and stamped it. The appellant Haigang Credit Cooperative raised an objection to this statement by Liu Xinglin and applied for an expert examination to determine whether the date written on the "Certificate" or the affixed official seal came first. The court entrusted document examiners of the Criminal Technology Division of the Beijing Public Security Bureau Criminal Investigation Corps with the examination. The conclusion was that the order of formation of the printed seal impression and the date writing on the submitted "Certificate" was that the date was formed first, and the printed seal impression was formed later. Haigang Credit Cooperative did not object to the authenticity of the deposit certificate of RMB 259,936.6 newly submitted by Liu Xinglin and acknowledged that it was not included in the deposit amount determined in the first instance.

The Hebei High People's Court held:

The nature of this case should be a deposit dispute. The deposit certificate of RMB 259,936.6 submitted by the appellant Liu Xinglin during the second instance, to which the appellant Haigang Credit Cooperative raised no objection, should be confirmed. The disputed amount between the parties should be changed from the RMB 1,487,800 determined in the first instance, plus this deposit, to RMB 1,747,736.6. As for the "Certificate" issued by the former Mafang Credit Cooperative on July 16, 1998, the expert examination confirmed that the date was formed first and the printed seal impression was formed later, and the seal was authentic, which was consistent with Liu Xinglin's statement regarding the source of this documentary evidence. Therefore, it should be confirmed as having legal effect. Haigang Credit Cooperative's argument that the amount of debt mentioned in the "Certificate" was inconsistent with the result of the later audit and thus the content of the "Certificate" was untrue, used to deny the validity of the "Certificate," lacked sufficient reason. Haigang Credit Cooperative's appeal that the cooperative's deposit and withdrawal procedures complied with the bank's regulation that depositors withdraw money by seal, not by personal signature, could not submit the corresponding legal basis or the agreement on this issue between the cooperative and the depositor Liu Xinglin; its claim that Liu Xinglin was aware of all deposits and withdrawals also could not submit evidence proving such awareness. Haigang Credit Cooperative also argued in its appeal that Liu Xinglin's act of leaving his seal with Cheng Xiuli constituted an authorization to Cheng, and if there was any harmful act, it should be Cheng who is responsible to Liu, not the credit cooperative. It was found that when Cheng Xiuli accepted Liu Xinglin's seal, her identity was that of the director of Mafang Credit Cooperative, who was then representing Mafang Credit Cooperative in safeguarding Liu Xinglin's deposits. This identity determined that Cheng Xiuli could not simultaneously accept Liu Xinglin's entrustment to act as an agent for Liu Xinglin in handling deposit matters. The grounds of appeal by Haigang Credit Cooperative could not be established and were not supported.

Based on all the evidence in this case, it can be determined that the appellant Liu Xinglin still has RMB 1,747,736.6 in unwithdrawn deposits with the appellant Haigang Credit Cooperative, and Haigang Credit Cooperative has the obligation to honor this amount. The calculation of interest on this amount at the personal demand deposit rate in the first instance judgment was improper and should be modified. Liu Xinglin's appeal was meritorious and should be supported. Accordingly, the Hebei High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 26, 2001:

1. The civil judgment of first instance is reversed;

2. The appellant Haigang Credit Cooperative shall, within 10 days after this judgment is served, pay the appellant Liu Xinglin a deposit of RMB 1,747,736.6 and interest. Interest shall be calculated from September 1, 1998, until the actual date of payment of the principal, at the corresponding period's loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China.

The allocation of litigation costs for the first instance remains unchanged. The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 20,184, to be borne by the appellant Haigang Credit Cooperative.
